This schematic summarizes the mechanistic link between stroke and subsequent sleep disorders via gut-brain axis dysregulation

This schematic summarizes the mechanistic link between stroke and subsequent sleep disorders via gut-brain axis dysregulation. Following a stroke, brain damage induces HPA axis activation and autonomic dysfunction, which in turn disrupts the intestinal barrier and microbiota balance. The resulting gut leakage permits LPS translocation, triggering systemic inflammation through the TLR4/NF-kB pathway. This inflammation ultimately causes astrocyte dysfunction and sleep disturbances. The graphic also highlights potential intervention points, such as microbiota reconstitution and anti-inflammatory strategies

Research progress on the role of microbiome-immune-neurotransmitter network in post-stroke sleep disorders (2025) Wanting Shi, et al. Front Aging Neurosci. 2025 Dec 01;17(NA). Figure: F0.
